leave.title: Leave without saving?
leave.body: Your changes on this page are not saved and will be lost.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.intro: Use the same account as for the classic openmediavault interface.
signIn.tooManyAttemptsBody: Wait a few minutes, then try again. Each failed attempt makes the wait longer, so trying again straight away does not help.
signIn.lockedTitle: Check the password before trying again
signIn.lockedBody: After repeated failed sign-ins the server can lock an account. Waiting does not unlock it, and this page cannot either. Ask another administrator to unlock the account. If it is the only administrator account, someone with access to the server's own screen and keyboard has to reset it there.
signIn.endedNotice: Your session ended, so you were signed out. Sign in again to carry on where you were.
signIn.challengeExpiredNotice: The code step took too long or was interrupted, so the sign-in was cancelled. Sign in again.
signIn.rejectedBody: Check the user name and password, then try again.
signIn.unreachableBody: Check that the server is switched on and connected to the network, then try again.

totp.title: Enter your code
totp.intro: Open the authenticator app you set up for {{username}} and enter the code it shows now.
totp.hint: The code changes every 30 seconds. You can paste it.
totp.invalid: Enter the 6 digits your authenticator app shows.
totp.tooManyAttemptsBody: Wait a few minutes, then enter the code your app shows at that moment. Each wrong code makes the wait longer.
totp.rejectedBody: Enter the code your authenticator app shows now. Each code works for only 30 seconds.

unsupported.title: Finish signing in with the classic interface
unsupported.body: Your password was accepted, but this account has a second sign-in step that this interface does not support yet. Sign in with the classic interface instead; it opens in a new tab.

signOut.failedBody: You are still signed in. Try again in a moment.

idle.title: Are you still there?
idle.body: Nothing has happened here for a while, so the server will sign you out in {{time}}.
idle.stayFailed: Could not reach the server. Try again, or sign out.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: There is no page at this address. It may have moved, or the address may be mistyped.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.signedInAs: You are signed in as {{username}}, with {{role}} rights.
dashboard.signedInRole: You are signed in with {{role}} rights.
dashboard.loadFailed: Could not read the system information.
dashboard.stale: Could not update since {{time}}. The figures may be out of date.

system.title: System
system.name: Name
system.updatesNone: None found at the last check
system.updatesLink: Review updates in the classic interface
system.moreLink: More system details in the classic interface

usage.title: Usage
usage.loadHint: How many tasks wait for the processor on average. Below {{cores}}, the number of processor cores, the NAS keeps up.

attention.label: Needs attention
attention.restart: A restart is needed to finish installing updates. Restarting is in the classic interface, in the power menu at the top right.
attention.clock: The NAS clock and this computer's clock differ by {{duration}}. If the NAS clock is wrong, schedules and logs will be too.
attention.clockLink: Check Date and time in the classic interface

user.title: This NAS
user.account: To change your password or your details, go to your account.

classicOnly.body: This page is not in the new interface yet. It works as before in the classic interface.
classicOnly.addOnsBody: Pages that installed plugins add are only in the classic interface for now.

adminOnly.body: Only administrators can open this page. Your account is a normal user account.

routeError.title: This page could not be shown
routeError.body: Something went wrong while opening this page. Try again, or go back to the dashboard.

httpNotice.label: Connection notice
httpNotice.body: This connection is not encrypted. Passwords and settings you send can be read by others on the network.
httpNotice.userBody: Ask an administrator to turn on HTTPS.

pending.label: Pending changes
pending.messageUnknown: Saved changes are waiting to be applied.
pending.applyFailed: Applying the changes failed. They are still saved and waiting.
pending.undoFailed: Undoing the changes failed. They are still saved and waiting.
pending.applyBody: The saved settings are put into effect now. The services listed below are reconfigured and may restart.
pending.connectionWarning: This includes the network, the web server or certificates, so this page may lose its connection while they restart. If it stops responding, wait a minute, then reload the page.
pending.undoBody: The saved changes to <list></list> are discarded. The settings go back to how they are on the server now.
pending.undoBodyAll: The saved changes are discarded. The settings go back to how they are on the server now.

tasks.selected: Output selected. Press Ctrl+C to copy.
tasks.endFailed: The task failed. The server's account of what happened is above.

about.title: About this interface
about.body: This is an unofficial community plugin that adds a new web interface to openmediavault. It is not made by the openmediavault project, and it changes nothing about how openmediavault works or how secure it is.

checklist.title: Set up your NAS
checklist.intro: A few things to check after installing. Each item is read from the NAS's current settings.

password.title: Change the factory password
password.body: openmediavault is installed with a password that anyone can look up. If it has not been changed yet, change it now. This page cannot check whether it has been.
password.bodyOtherAdmin: openmediavault is installed with a password for the admin account that anyone can look up. This page cannot check whether it has been changed. To change it, sign in as admin and open Your account.

https.title: Use a secure connection (HTTPS)
https.doneOnHttp: HTTPS is on, but this page was opened without it.
https.secureNoLink: Open this page with an address that starts with https://.
https.notDone: HTTPS is off. The notice at the top of the page says why that matters. Turning it on needs a certificate, which the classic interface can create.
https.link: Open Web interface settings in the classic interface
https.readFailed: Could not read the web interface settings.

email.title: Get email alerts
email.off: Alerts are off. Turn them on to hear about failing disks, full file systems and available updates. You need the details of an email account the NAS can send from.
email.incomplete: Alerts are on, but some details are missing, so none can be sent.
email.applyHint: After saving there, apply the changes, then send a test email.
email.link: Open Notifications in the classic interface
email.readFailed: Could not read the email alert settings.

updates.title: Install updates
updates.none: No updates were found the last time the NAS looked. This page cannot tell when that was, so check for updates once to be sure.
updates.link: Open Updates in the classic interface

name.title: Name of your NAS
name.body: Your NAS is called <name></name>. Other computers on your network find it by this name.
name.link: Change it in the classic interface

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.body: Time zone: <zone></zone>. Schedules, logs and the clock use it.
timezone.ntpOn: The clock is set automatically from the internet.
timezone.ntpOff: The clock is not set automatically.
timezone.link: Change it in the classic interface
timezone.readFailed: Could not read the date and time settings.

checklist.hideHint: Hides it for every administrator, and hides the classic interface's welcome panel too.
checklist.hideBody: It is hidden for every administrator, on every computer, and the classic interface's welcome panel goes too. This interface cannot show it again.

ssh.title: SSH
ssh.intro: SSH lets you sign in to the NAS from another computer and type commands. It is for advanced tasks; most people never need it.
ssh.pendingOnArrival: Saved SSH settings are waiting to be applied. The form shows the saved settings, which are not in effect yet.
ssh.enableHint: Each person also needs SSH access on their own account, which is set under Users.
ssh.offNote: The settings below are used when SSH is on.
ssh.portHint: The number SSH programs connect to. The usual one is 22; if you change it, tell your SSH program the new number.
ssh.portRequired: Enter a port number. The usual one is 22.
ssh.portRange: Enter a whole number from 1 to 65535.
ssh.portInUse: Port {{port}} is already used by this web interface. Choose another, such as 22.
ssh.password: Allow signing in with a password
ssh.key: Allow signing in with a key
ssh.keyHint: A key is a file on your computer that proves who you are, with no password to guess. Keys are added to each account under Users.
ssh.root: Allow the root account to sign in
ssh.rootHint: root is the built-in account with full control of the NAS. It is safer to leave this off and sign in with your own account.
ssh.forwardingHint: Lets someone signed in pass other network traffic through the NAS. Leave it off unless you use it.
ssh.compressionHint: Can speed up slow connections, at the cost of some processor time.
ssh.extraHint: These lines are added as they are to the SSH server's configuration file. A mistake can stop SSH from starting, so leave this empty unless you know you need it.
ssh.warnNoMethod: With both ways of signing in turned off, nobody can sign in over SSH. To stop SSH, turn it off at the top instead.
ssh.warnTurningOff: After you apply this, new SSH connections are refused. Anything that connects over SSH, such as a backup from another computer, stops working.
ssh.warnRootPassword: The root account can sign in with only a password. Anyone who guesses it controls the NAS. Turn off root sign-in, or allow keys only.
ssh.warnKeysOnly: Only people with a key on their account can sign in now. Check that yours is added before you apply.
ssh.saved: Saved. The changes take effect when you apply them in the band at the top of the page.
ssh.saveFailed: The SSH settings were not saved.
ssh.loadFailed: Could not read the SSH settings.

sharedFolders.title: Shared folders
sharedFolders.intro: Folders on your disks that other computers can reach over the network. To add, change or delete one, use the classic interface for now.
sharedFolders.addClassic: Add a shared folder in the classic interface
sharedFolders.usedNote: In use: a network share, backup job or other setting refers to this folder. Which one is not reported.

reason.ENOENT: Folder not found. Its disk may be disconnected or not mounted.
reason.ENOTDIR: The path leads to a file, not a folder.
reason.ENOENT_DB_MNTENT: Its file system is no longer set up on this NAS.

sharedFolders.rollUp_one: {{count}} of {{total}} shared folders cannot be reached.
sharedFolders.rollUp_other: {{count}} of {{total}} shared folders cannot be reached.
sharedFolders.searchHint: Search looks at every detail of a folder, including some not shown in the table, so a short word such as "ok" or "1" can match more folders than you expect.
sharedFolders.loadFailed: Could not read the shared folders.
sharedFolders.empty: There are no shared folders yet. A shared folder is a folder on one of your disks that other computers can reach over the network.

account.title: Your account
account.name: User name
account.commentHint: A note about this account, such as your full name. Administrators see it in the list of users.
account.commentInvalid: A description cannot contain a colon (:) or a line break.
account.emailHint: Messages the NAS sends to your account are forwarded here.
account.emailInvalid: Enter an email address like name@example.com, or leave it empty.
account.adminNote: This page cannot change an administrator's details. Email alerts about the NAS are set up under Notifications.
account.adminNoteLink: Open Notifications in the classic interface
account.lockedNote: Your administrator has locked this account's details and password. Ask them if something needs changing.
account.passwordIntro: The new password works straight away; there is nothing to apply. It is the same account everywhere, so it also becomes your password for the classic interface and, if you use them, for shared folders on other computers.
account.newPasswordHint: Use a long password that you do not use anywhere else.
account.passwordMismatch: The two passwords are not the same. Type them again.
account.passwordChangedLine: Password changed. Use the new password the next time you sign in.
account.pendingNote: Changes are now waiting to be applied. Apply them with the band at the top of the page.
account.noKeys: No SSH keys are added to this account.
account.noKeysUser: An administrator adds them under Users.
account.noKeysAdminLink: Add keys under Users in the classic interface
